title: Executive Readout (Draft): Internal Unit Economics Dashboard (v1) — Blended $/1M Output Tokens
content:
Audience: ELT + Eng/Product/Finance leadership
Date: 2025-02-24
Presenter(s): Marissa Cole (Product), Dylan Brooks (Eng), Laura Bennett (Finance)

1) Executive summary (TL;DR)
We built an internal Unit Economics dashboard to make inference cost drivers visible and actionable across Product, Engineering, and Finance. The dashboard’s primary KPI is blended $/1M output tokens, with first-class drilldowns by model (incl. version + quantization profile where available), region, and customer tier (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise).

Why it matters: We are increasingly competing on serving economics (latency, reliability, cost). Today, we do not have a single trusted, finance-aligned view of unit cost that is: (a) consistent across deployments, (b) debuggable when it moves, and (c) operationalized enough to be used for quarterly KPI reporting without manual heroics.

What’s new with v1:
- A finance-aligned, versioned definition of “blended $/1M output tokens” with reconciliation steps and explicit inclusion/exclusion rules.
- Drilldowns that highlight outliers and connect them to runtime signals (cache hit rate, batching efficiency, output length, streaming vs non-streaming, quantization profile).
- Data quality checks + SLOs + an on-call playbook so the metric is dependable for exec reporting.

Current state (as of this draft):
- v1 dashboard is available behind internal feature flag + RBAC allowlist.
- Token metering parity work for streaming has landed; reconciliation report is in place with known limitations.
- We can already see a small set of repeatable cost drivers (region mix, tier mix, output length distribution, cache/batching utilization) and identify where instrumentation gaps previously masked cost regressions.

Key takeaway: The dashboard is now good enough to guide engineering prioritization and support Finance’s QTD reporting, with clear caveats. Next quarter’s roadmap is focused on (1) tightening reconciliation and confidence indicators, (2) expanding drilldowns (model version/route), and (3) wiring “measurement → action” workflows for Optimize and runtime teams.

2) The business case: why now
We need a shared, trusted unit economics metric because:
- Optimization is now multi-team: runtime (batching/caching), infra (capacity/region), applied ML (quantization profiles), and product (routing/fallback policies). Without a common metric + diagnosis path, we make local changes that are hard to evaluate and easy to misattribute.
- Customer demand is rising: multiple accounts (esp. enterprise and cost-sensitive mid-market) ask for cost transparency by model/region. Even though v1 is internal-only, we need the internal truth before we can safely externalize.
- Exec reporting requires stability: FP&A needs QTD and quarter-over-quarter visibility that reconciles with spend inputs and metering. Historically, we’ve done this via spreadsheets + one-off queries, which doesn’t scale and introduces trust issues.

What changed since last quarter:
- We now have enough metering and tagging infrastructure (model IDs, region normalization, tier derivation, quant profile tagging) to support reliable drilldowns without runaway cardinality.
- Finance has published and signed off on a versioned methodology for applying the GPU cost rate card and allocating shared overhead/idle capacity.

3) What shipped in v1 (scope recap)
3.1 Metric definition (finance-aligned)
Primary metric: blended $/1M output tokens
- Numerator: allocated inference cost over a time window (GPU compute + supported overhead allocations; see ADR-034 + Finance methodology).
- Denominator: metered output tokens for eligible inference routes/models (with explicit inclusion/exclusion rules).
- Dimensions: model (and model version / quantization profile where available), region (normalized), customer tier.

Finance alignment notes:
- Rate card source is versioned; methodology is stable across a reporting period.
- Reconciliation report compares aggregated dashboard totals vs billing/spend views with a documented tolerance band and common causes for deltas.

3.2 Dashboard experience (internal Console)
- Default landing: blended $/1M output tokens trend for selected time range (daily view default; hourly available for investigations).
- Breakdown tabs: Top-N by model / region / tier with comparisons vs prior period.
- Drilldown: click into a segment to see contributing signals (cache hit rate, batching efficiency, avg output length, streaming share, quant profile).
- Empty/error states: explicit messaging when data confidence is reduced (missing dims, lagging ingestion, etc.).

3.3 Operationalization
- Pipeline SLOs: data freshness + completeness targets with paging alerts.
- Data quality checks: missing dimension coverage, sudden token drops/spikes, unexpected cardinality growth.
- On-call playbook: validation queries, backfill steps, escalation guidance (including when to loop in Finance).

4) Early findings (from dogfooding + first weeks of data)
These are “directionally true” findings; we are intentionally avoiding over-precision until the confidence indicator and reconciliation loop have been run for a full month-end close.

4.1 Streaming paths were undercounting output tokens prior to fix
- We identified systematic undercounting on streaming responses that made blended cost appear worse (numerator steady, denominator too low).
- Fix landed and is now covered by regression tests + a canary check.
- Impact: improved trust in the dashboard trend line; reduced false-positive “cost spike” investigations.

4.2 Region mix is a first-order driver of blended unit cost
- The dashboard makes region-driven cost differences legible without manual joins across infra billing sources.
- We’ve already used this view to answer internal questions like “Is this a true per-token regression or just more traffic shifting to a higher-cost region?”
- Immediate operational benefit: Support/CS can be guided internally on suspected region-driven spikes (e.g., eu-west reports) with a repeatable analysis path.

4.3 Tier mix and idle allocation can distort blended comparisons if not labeled
- Dedicated/private tiers behave differently from hosted/self-serve due to reservation/commit structure and idle treatment.
- Without explicit tier filters, blended aggregates can move due to tier mix shifts rather than serving regressions.
- Action taken: UI defaults now bias toward “hosted/self-serve” for day-to-day engineering investigations; Finance view remains “all tiers” with a clearly labeled tier composition panel.

4.4 Cache hit rate and batching efficiency correlate with cost in the expected direction, but signal quality varies by route
- On some routes/models, cache hit rate is a clean explanatory variable for cost; on others, instrumentation quality and workload mix obscure the relationship.
- We need to tighten definitions (e.g., prefix vs KV cache, request eligibility) and ensure the dashboard reports “coverage %” for each signal.

4.5 Quantization profile tagging is working for a subset; we need broader coverage and guardrails
- Where quant_profile is present, the breakdown is already useful for identifying wins that didn’t translate to the expected cost improvement (often due to batching/caching interactions or routing differences).
- Next: enforce allowed values, expand instrumentation coverage, and connect to quality guardrails so cost wins don’t silently degrade output quality.

5) What we can say to execs today vs what we should caveat
Reliable now (v1):
- Trends and relative comparisons within a consistent dimension slice (e.g., same tier + region) are usable for prioritization.
- Outlier detection for major regressions (token drops, missing dimensions, sudden cost jumps) is operationalized.
- Finance-aligned methodology exists and is implemented; reconciliation report provides structured investigation when deltas occur.

Caveats (explicit in the UI and in Finance methodology notes):
- Month-end close and rate-card updates: we version the rate card; period-over-period comparisons must note methodology version.
- Idle and shared overhead allocations: blended cost is not the same as marginal cost; we need a clearer UI distinction.
- Some secondary signals (cache/batching) have incomplete coverage; the dashboard should not be used to set precise per-team OKRs on those sub-metrics yet.

6) Next quarter roadmap (v1.1)
Goal: increase trust + actionability, then expand use cases.

6.1 Trust + reporting readiness
- Confidence indicator: per-slice data coverage + freshness + reconciliation status shown inline (e.g., “High/Medium/Low confidence” with why).
- Stronger reconciliation workflows: scheduled monthly reconciliation package for FP&A, plus an audit trail of rate-card version + allocation parameters.
- Timezone/day-boundary alignment: ensure Finance reporting periods match hourly rollups (reduce “off-by-one day” confusion).

6.2 Deeper drilldowns for faster diagnosis
- Model version and alias handling: consistent grouping of model aliases (marketing name vs internal ID) with the ability to drill to version when needed.
- Route-level breakdown (guarded): allow internal drilldowns by route/template while maintaining cardinality and privacy constraints.
- “Explain this change” view: show top contributors to week-over-week change (mix shift vs per-unit regression).

6.3 Connect measurement to action (Optimize + Runtime)
- Regression alerts tied to rollouts: flag unit-cost deltas during model rollouts / quant profile changes.
- Suggested levers: when cost moves, recommend likely actions (e.g., batching config changes, caching eligibility, quant profile selection) with links to runbooks.
- Quality guardrails integration: attach eval/quality status to quant profile comparisons so teams don’t optimize cost blindly.

6.4 Access controls and internal comms
- Expand allowlist to Finance/Product/Eng managers + oncall responders; keep sensitive drilldowns restricted.
- Publish a short internal “How to interpret blended cost” guide and add it to the dashboard help panel.

7) Open risks + mitigations
Risk A: Reconciliation deltas undermine trust (“dashboard doesn’t match billing/spend”)
- Mitigation: keep a single finance-owned methodology, version rate cards, run a formal reconciliation cadence, and show reconciliation status in the UI.

Risk B: High-cardinality dimensions degrade pipeline stability
- Mitigation: strict cardinality guardrails + allowed-value constraints (especially quant_profile, route identifiers) and automated alerting.

Risk C: Misinterpretation of blended vs marginal cost drives wrong decisions
- Mitigation: UI labeling + default views by tier, plus an “interpretation” panel that highlights mix effects and idle allocation.

Risk D: Data completeness regressions (especially streaming or new gateway paths)
- Mitigation: keep the canary + regression tests for output token metering; SRE-owned SLOs with clear escalation.

Risk E: Performance of drilldowns (slow queries reduces adoption)
- Mitigation: materialized views/partitioning; caching on common queries; separate “live” vs “finance” views with documented freshness.

8) Decisions/asks
For ELT approval this quarter:
1) Confirm that “blended $/1M output tokens” (v1 methodology) is the metric we’ll use for FY2026 quarterly KPI reporting, with the stated caveats.
2) Greenlight 1 additional quarter of investment (v1.1) to reach month-end close readiness + confidence indicators + deeper drilldowns.
3) Align on internal access policy: keep internal-only for now; revisit externalization after we have a stable quarter of reconciled reporting.

9) Appendix: definitions (one-paragraph)
Blended $/1M output tokens = (allocated inference cost over window, using versioned GPU rate card + agreed allocations for shared overhead/idle) / (eligible metered output tokens over the same window). “Blended” reflects the total cost of serving across a slice, not marginal per-request cost; mix shifts (tier/region/workload) can move the metric even when serving efficiency is unchanged.

Notes to self (drafting):
- Confirm which charts Finance wants in the FY2026 KPI pack (QTD view + prior quarter comps).
- Add one anonymized screenshot callout list once Design approves final formatting/rounding.
- Validate current RBAC allowlist and whether we can include CS leadership for internal customer investigations.
